clue.text: One's disparaged for going to work in small taxi

definitions.text: One's disparaged for going to work
definitions.note: read as 'one who is disparaged for working during a strike'

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone is sneered at for commuting to their job in a tiny taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to work' hides the real sense: crossing a picket line while colleagues are on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the insulting term for a worker who breaks a strike, so such a person is scorned by fellow workers.

clue.text: Source of minerals almost absent in this state

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is left off

blocks.note: ore is rock from which minerals are extracted
someone absent has gone

explanation.surface: A US state is said to lack the rocks that yield minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Doctor finding new ruler in bed

indicators.note: one thing lying in another sits inside it, so the first pieces go inside the last

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a sultan rules a Muslim state
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A doctor discovers an unfamiliar monarch lying in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a consultant is a senior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a senior hospital specialist, which makes the role a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Going on horseback in part of Yorkshire

blocks.note: first meaning: travelling mounted on a horse
second meaning: one of the historic divisions of a northern English county

explanation.surface: Someone travels by horse through a region of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large English county, was historically split into three Ridings: North, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of travelling mounted and the name of each old administrative division of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Austrian dressed ornately

indicators.note: dressing something up arranges it differently, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Austrian wears elaborate, showy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a region of western Austria, so its people and things are Austrian.

clue.text: Duke is heading for criminal record

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written
first letter of criminal

explanation.surface: An aristocrat seems bound to acquire a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal record' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits there: criminal supplies one letter and record is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the flat vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Awful grime around WC getting darker

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a loo is a WC, a lavatory

explanation.surface: Filthy dirt spreading round a toilet makes it look ever dingier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomier describes a place with less light, so it is a comparative synonym of darker.

clue.text: Has Jesse lost energy?

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is taken out of the name

blocks.note: Jesse Owens was the American sprinter who won four golds at the 1936 Olympics
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A question asks whether someone called Jesse has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first name appears; the solver must supply the athlete's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it as a possession, so owns matches has.

clue.text: Feline killer is something unusual

blocks.note: first meaning: from the proverb that says it killed the cat
second meaning: an odd or rare object

explanation.walkthrough: The first half relies on the proverb about what killed the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the inquisitiveness that the saying blames for a cat's death, and also a rare or strange object.

clue.text: Home rule for a sort of relation

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Self-government is proposed for some kind of relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home rule' looks like a single political term, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent.

clue.text: Turn back in vehicle that's not what it seems

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from its end
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone turns round inside a vehicle that is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means sham or counterfeit, describing something that is not genuine.

clue.text: Annoyed after golf club gets German award

indicators.note: after says which part comes second, so the word for annoyed follows the club

blocks.note: an iron is a kind of golf club
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone angry at a golf club is given a German decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a Prussian and German military decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Fielder — one of daddy's six?

blocks.note: first meaning: a cricket fielding position deep on the leg side behind the batsman
second meaning: a limb of the daddy-..., the crane fly, which has six

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, long leg is a fielding position near the boundary. A daddy-long-legs is a crane fly, an insect with six spindly legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a cricketer's fielding station and a single limb of the six-legged crane fly.

clue.text: Popular as door opener

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the start of the word is used

blocks.note: as and like both mean in the manner of
first letter of door

explanation.surface: Something well liked is treated as the thing that opens a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Door opener' looks like a key or handle; it is just the first letter of door.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular is widely liked, so the past participle stands for it.

clue.text: Joy has broken toenail

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Joy has damaged a toenail.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy reads as a woman's name at the start of the sentence, but it is the plain noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness, a close synonym of joy.

clue.text: Loyalty, for example, in union

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
an alliance is a union

explanation.surface: Loyalty is cited as one example of what keeps a union together.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful loyalty owed to a ruler, country or cause.

clue.text: Negative remark about saint is offensive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remark goes round the next piece

blocks.note: nay is an old word for no
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A critical comment about a saint causes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or hurtful, which is what offensive describes.

clue.text: Country singer (Irish) seen by king

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Enya is the Irish singer known for 'Orinoco Flow'

explanation.surface: An Irish country music singer is spotted near a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country singer' reads as a music genre, but Country stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is a nation in East Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: With long novel one's late to bed

definitions.note: read as 'one who goes late to bed'

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone up reading a long book goes to bed late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being read, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who habitually stays up until late at night.

clue.text: One imprisoned for fraud

blocks.note: first meaning: a convict, in short
second meaning: a swindle or trick

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone jailed for fraud; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is slang for a convict and also means a confidence trick or swindle.

clue.text: Crikey!  Is lad mixing drinks?

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like crikey
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find a boy making cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixing drinks' reads as bartending, but mixing acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordials are sweet fruit drinks, or liqueurs, so they are drinks.

clue.text: Fun with birds

blocks.note: first meaning: pranks or bits of mischief
second meaning: small songbirds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a jolly day out birdwatching; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are both lighthearted escapades and a family of songbirds such as the skylark.

clue.text: Lassie from Sirius?

blocks.note: first meaning: a canine film and TV celebrity, the collie of the Lassie films
second meaning: the brightest star in the night sky, in the constellation Canis Major

explanation.walkthrough: Lassie also means a girl, which makes the clue look like a girl from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous screen dog is literally a dog star, while Sirius has long been called the Dog Star.

clue.text: Tidying mess, showing self-respect

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so these letters are thrown out of their arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Clearing up clutter shows that someone has pride in themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignity is a sense of pride and self-worth, which is what self-respect means.

clue.text: Desperate character is seen with hot pastry

blocks.note: Desperate Dan is the cow-pie-eating strongman of the British comic The Dandy
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A frantic person is spotted holding a warm pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a long-running British comic-strip character, so 'Desperate character' names him rather than describing anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet yeast pastry, short for Danish pastry.

clue.text: One with wheels — American or Greek high flyer

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
wheels is slang for a car
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A driver is either a US national or a Greek who flies high.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wax wings too close to the sun, so he was a literal high flyer.

clue.text: Object no one brought back after camping?

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so these words are read from the end
after places the reversed piece behind the camping piece

blocks.note: someone camping is in a tent
no plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks what nobody returned after a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb meaning to protest; it is the noun meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is an aim or purpose, the sense in which intention is a synonym.

clue.text: An old Peruvian of a certain caste

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters come from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters span the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian belonged to a particular social class.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits nicely, since the Inca ruling class was itself a privileged caste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people whose empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Numbers provided with hospital food

blocks.note: nos is the abbreviation for numbers
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Patients are given numbered portions of hospital meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Gather for a service

blocks.note: taken as written
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A call for people to assemble for worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Gather sounds like a congregation assembling; it is the verb meaning to collect.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate or collect things together, the sense of gather.

clue.text: Where tools may be kept or discarded

blocks.note: first meaning: a garden hut for storage
second meaning: cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether tools are stored or thrown away; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small storage hut and is also the past tense of the verb meaning to cast off.

clue.text: Herd heard in port

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word is taken by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a herd is a group of cows

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle can be heard in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing port on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast; Herd and heard play on sound too.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes is a harbour town famous for its yachting regatta, so it is a port.

clue.text: As to clues being cracked, it's a hopeless endeavour

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver complains that trying to crack these clues is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' sounds like solving clues, but here it means broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an effort or aim that cannot possibly succeed, so it is hopeless.
